Herd immunity functions similarly to a digital firewall in computer security. Just as a firewall protects a network by ensuring that enough computers are secured against malware, preventing an infected machine from spreading a virus to unprotected systems, herd immunity protects a population. When a sufficient number of people are immune to an infectious disease, the pathogen finds it difficult to spread from an infected individual to those who are not immune, thereby safeguarding the entire community.
